title: Processing a Self-Delimited Pair
statement: For either choice of the program parameter and all bit strings $u$ and $r$, there are a register assignment and an input position such that, on the input formed by doubling every bit of $u$, appending the separator $01$, and then appending $r$, the program starting at its scan label with register value $0$ and input position $0$ reaches a halted state with that register assignment and input position. It adds $r$ truncated to its first $|u|$ bits when the parameter is true, and $r$ with its first $|u|$ bits removed when the parameter is false; the run takes at most five times one more than the input length. This holds for every output string already printed.
hypotheses_covered: The program parameter is a Boolean choice
The input is the pair encoding of arbitrary bit strings $u$ and $r$
The input position starts at zero
